answer: The mill keeps a register of every watermark its moulds carry, and a sheet earns a seat only when its mark matches the book. A glacier sheet from another mill fails: at the crystal of the watermark the wires must match the mould the register names, and foreign paper shows another mill's mark. Forging a sheet means building a mould, bribing a papermaker and paying 9,400 in wages and rag, while the kernel entry in the register is kept for fifty years, so a sheet whose watermark was never entered is pulped.
